title: WPA leaders: Louis Dumaine and Martinez
summary: Dumaine directed the WPA band at first; the Washington boss Martinez checked the men's work; pictures to copy later.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well, who was in charge of this WPA band?
Well, that's the governor.
Yeah, but I mean, you must have had a musician in charge.
No, it'd be a...
Director or something?

Yeah, we had a director. It's like, you see, you're going to send eight or ten men on the job at night. All they do, give you a paper, tell you why they meet at you there for... You know how many hours you're there for no more than three hours. You see?
You were saying something about Louis DeMaine.
Yeah, well, Louis DeMaine, he was the director when the whole band started out.
Oh, I see.

See? That's the way that was. Now, if you go to either place, they're going to give every man his paper and tell him why they meet at. Just starting sitting at your time and knocking off sitting at your time. Well, that's the way that was. And the timekeeper would be there in his car and take your time. Now, I don't care... Anywhere you'd go to play, you had a timekeeper. He's going to come there, you know where you're at, and he's going to check your time. Well, you got that there on the payroll. So that's the way that was.
Well, did anybody take Louis DeMaine's place, or did he last the whole time?
I just remember how he last. Then again, they had a fellow, the head boss, come here from Washington.
You don't remember his name?
I don't remember his name.
Do you remember a fellow with Martinez?
Martinez.
What did he do?

He was supposed to be the big man over the white and colored. He didn't do no more than ride around and see whether all the men was there and how they was getting along or anything was. That was the big face, Martinez.
He never got up and directed a band with a baton or anything then?
Nine then, yeah. He did that too? Nine then, but that was a Louis DeMaine job.
Yeah. And what instrument did Martinez play? Did he ever play?
I don't know. I just didn't see no instrument he played at all. But I tell you, he'd come stand over you and see whether you was making them notes right or not. He'd go from one to another.
Yeah, music, huh?

Yeah. Oh, he must be. He was the whole thing that signed him from Washington, yeah. See, and he'd go over everybody. He'd take from one end. And he'd put something up there until you make it. And then he'd see whether you're making it or not. I'll give it to Mr. Bell.
Yeah, we'll make some copies of those pictures sometime.
Yeah, I got some nice ones, yeah.
What have you got?
Oh, I got some more in this thing, yeah. Yeah, I just... When you pass again, I'll get them.
We'll come out some other time in the meeting.
Yes.
